text:
Alex Newhook has stepped into a bigger role in Montreal with Ivan Demidov and Chris Kreider out, playing beside Jake Evans in Kreider's old spot. He has six goals and 12 points in 24 games, and his goals match his chances almost exactly.

The worry is the other end. Montreal takes 41% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), 13 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 9% of forwards last season for what his team created with him on, so this is not new. He does exit his zone cleanly, 59% with possession in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and he set up Zachary Bolduc's power-play goal against Philadelphia. A Stanley Cup winner in Colorado in 2022, he is 25. Watch where he lands once the Canadiens are healthy and Dylan Larkin settles in.
